bull.b: The shift to strongly positive operating and free cash flow provides DraftKings with internal funding for product development, customer acquisition, and market expansion. This improves financial resilience and reduces reliance on external capital as the core business scales.

Rapid customer acquisition combined with higher revenue per unique customer indicates improving engagement and monetization, not growth dependent solely on adding users. Sustained unit-economics improvement can support revenue expansion and operating leverage over coming quarters.

The rapid adoption of Predictions adds a potentially incremental product to DraftKings’ existing sportsbook ecosystem, while combos and broader sports coverage deepen usage. Continued product development could diversify engagement and increase lifetime value if regulatory access remains available.

bear.b: Debt exceeding three times equity leaves DraftKings more sensitive to earnings volatility and reduces flexibility for investment or unexpected operating pressure. Although cash generation has improved, elevated leverage can constrain capital allocation and increase dependence on sustained business performance.

The return to a net loss and continued negative operating profit show that improved scale has not yet produced consistently durable bottom-line profitability. This weakens earnings quality and leaves future results exposed to promotional spending, outcomes variability, and investment requirements.

NBA restrictions remove selected wagering opportunities from DraftKings’ sportsbook, including some parlay and player-related markets. Repeated or broader limits could reduce product breadth, constrain handle and hold opportunities, and increase the importance of alternative betting and gaming products.
